risks.description: Accepted residual risk: the AppleScriptSecurityFilter is a regex denylist applied after comment and string-literal stripping. Four documented bypass classes (string-concat reconstruction, Unicode normalization, dynamic run script with tell-application return value, comment-split that re-forms the keyword) are not statically detectable.

props.name: re-evaluation-criterion
props.value: Swift AST parser availability or observed in-the-wild bypass

remediations.description: Continue to rely on the audit hook + TCC + MCP host gates; revisit when fuzz coverage data exists.

tasks.description: Measured bypass-class coverage from the AppleScript fuzz harness reaches ≥80% of documented bypass classes; results published as a CI artifact and reviewed by the security owner.
tasks.title: STORY-025 fuzz harness operational

tasks.description: Security owner reviews docs/SECURITY.md §4.1 bypass class list against published AppleScript research and incident reports; new classes are added or the item closes if all four are addressed.
tasks.title: Quarterly re-review of bypass class catalog

remediations.title: Compensating monitoring plan (§4.1)

entries.description: Risk documented in SECURITY.md §4.1 with full justification; the four bypass classes are tracked individually as si-10_smt.bypass-* statements in oscal/component-definition.json.
entries.title: Risk accepted by security owner

risks.statement: Risk is accepted on the basis of compensating controls: STORY-024 audit hook (every invocation including filter-passes is logged with a tamper-evident chain), macOS TCC per-app automation gates, MCP host destructiveHint user-confirmation gate. Re-evaluation criterion: a credible Swift AST parser for AppleScript becomes available, or a post-incident review identifies an exploited bypass in this class.
risks.title: AppleScript security filter regex bypass class (SECURITY.md §4.1)

risks.description: Accepted residual risk: the 1 MB output truncation cap bounds bulk exfiltration but does not prevent a single targeted read (e.g. one password from Notes, one API key from a clipboard manager).

props.name: re-evaluation-criterion
props.value: Practical intent-classification approach to AI tool calls becomes available, or a deployer engagement requires per-tool data-classification gates

remediations.description: Watch for advances in agent intent classification that could enable per-tool data-classification gates.

tasks.description: Security owner publishes a short feasibility note on whether intent classification of agent-issued tool calls is tractable given current model capabilities and the project's threat model.
tasks.title: Intent-classification feasibility review

remediations.title: Intent-classification feasibility track (§4.2)

entries.description: Risk documented in SECURITY.md §4.2. Compensating control: 1 MB truncation cap with truncated:true flag; audit trail captures every invocation.
entries.title: Risk accepted by security owner

risks.statement: Justified because AI agents have legitimate reasons to read user data on the user's behalf; the user's choice to launch the server combined with the MCP host's confirmation gate is the consent model. The AuditRecorder captures the invocation (script SHA-256, timestamp, target apps), providing forensics for incident response.
risks.title: Single-secret exfiltration via stdout (SECURITY.md §4.2)

risks.description: Accepted residual risk: AppleScript scripts that build target app names dynamically (e.g. `tell application name1 & " " & name2`) cannot be statically extracted by AutomationPermissionChecker. The pre-flight check returns .skipped for these and the runtime TCC prompt becomes the gate; in CI this can manifest as a hung process waiting on a modal.

remediations.description: Verify the signed TCC grant helper is provisioned on all CI runners and that the integration suite exits non-zero (not hang) on a missing grant.

tasks.description: docs/INTEGRATION-CI-SETUP.md documents the signed-helper path; verify the helper is provisioned and the suite fails-fast on a missing grant rather than hanging.
tasks.title: TCC pre-grant verification on CI runners

remediations.title: Integration-suite TCC pre-grant verification (§4.3)

entries.description: Risk documented in SECURITY.md §4.3. Compensating control: pre-grant of automation permission to fixture apps in CI runners; runtime TCC is the production gate.
entries.title: Risk accepted by security owner

risks.statement: Mitigation: pre-grant automation permission for fixture apps used in integration tests; treat TCC prompts in production as an expected user touchpoint. Re-evaluation criterion: a reliable AppleScript identifier-resolution approach for dynamic names ships, or a CI hang attributable to this class is observed in the integration suite.
risks.title: Dynamic-name TCC prompts in CI (SECURITY.md §4.3)

risks.description: Acknowledged residual risk: per-record digital signatures would be stronger than the hash chain but signing requires key management; a stored key on the host is no harder to compromise than the host itself.

remediations.description: Watch for local HSM availability (Secure Enclave, smartcard, YubiKey) that could enable per-record AuditRecord signing.

tasks.description: Security owner publishes a short feasibility note on local HSM availability for per-record AuditRecord signing. Outcome either adds milestones or formalizes long-term acceptance.
tasks.title: HSM-signing feasibility review

remediations.title: HSM-signing feasibility track (§4.4)

entries.description: Risk documented in SECURITY.md §4.4. STORY-024 audit subsystem (chain + retention + off-host shipping) is the primary control; absence of HSM-backed signing is the residual.
entries.title: Risk accepted by security owner

risks.statement: STORY-024 chain + off-host shipping pair provides two independent corroborations (on-disk chain + remote sink's collected copy). Re-evaluation criterion: an HSM-backed signing path becoming available or a post-incident review identifying a class of tampering the chain misses.
risks.title: Audit log: no per-record HSM signing (SECURITY.md §4.4)

risks.description: Historical accepted risk: prior to Sprint 6, the AuditRecorder was an in-memory protocol seam suitable for development and CI but not for production.
risks.statement: Closed by STORY-024, which shipped a hash-chained, retained, off-host-shipping production sink (OSLog default, HTTP/syslog optional). The on-disk JSONL stream is append-only at the storage layer; AuditChainVerifier runs on server start, on every retention sweep, and on operator demand.
risks.title: Deferred production audit sink (SECURITY.md §4.4, closed by STORY-024)

risks.description: Auto-opened by oscal-emit whenever the AuditRecord stream contains a chain_verification_failure event. Each occurrence elevates the corresponding observation and adds a related-observation reference here so an assessor can pivot from the AR to the affected operational incident.

remediations.description: Operator runs verify_audit_chain, identifies the first-break record id, examines the chain offset, and either confirms benign cause or escalates per the playbook.

tasks.description: Operator runs verify_audit_chain, identifies the first-break record id, examines the chain offset, and either confirms benign cause (clock skew during archive rotation) or escalates per docs/AUDIT-LOG-OPERATIONS.md incident-response checklist.
tasks.title: Incident response: investigate latest chain break

remediations.title: Operator incident response on chain break

entries.description: Risk entry pre-allocated so oscal-emit can append related-observation references without synthesizing a new risk on every chain-break event. The status flips to closed once an operator clears the chain break.
entries.title: Risk opened (template)

risks.statement: Open until the operator verifies the chain break is benign (e.g. clock skew during archive rotation) or escalates per docs/AUDIT-LOG-OPERATIONS.md incident-response checklist. UUID matches OscalObservationEmitter.chainBreakRiskUuid so the emitter does not need runtime coordination to find this risk.
